gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +1872.6 (one group 41740.7, two groups 39868.1): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are only partly the DS / IED split (adjusted Rand 0.48, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 85% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

dbic_scale: very strong support for two groups

rule: Pooled over 18 recordings from 17 mice, in pooled raw units: the cluster whose centre has more 500–1000 Hz power is called IED: +18.6 dB against +10.5 dB for the other, which is called DS (3022 DS, 2015 IED; 48 assigned on 2 of 3 axes (half-width unresolved even at 50 ms)).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.

split_axis.unit: z, 0 at the midpoint, DS negative
